title: AI-Run Modern LaTeX Manuscript Workflow and Replication Packet
description:
Compact workflow and replication record for the Modern LaTeX Editions of Mathematics Manuscripts project. It documents the AI-run scan-to-TeX-to-translation-to-audit-to-publication workflow, including local source acquisition, OCR/math-OCR witness generation, source-image slicing, high-DPI object crops, TeX compilation, web review handoffs, GitHub mirroring, and Zenodo publication.

Latest update, 2026-06-25. Adds source-witness/public-surface and archive-scope guardrail addenda from current SGA, Noether, Gordan, Steinitz, Deligne, Cayley, and local sweep maintenance lessons, plus a failed-web salvage rule from Noether repair work. This update also adds the SGA5 and Weber find-verify-fix method snapshots. The SGA5 snapshot packages page-local discovery, independent source verification, deterministic old-string/new-string patching, compile gates, and the lesson that agent/swarm passes are finders rather than certifiers. The Weber snapshot adapts the same method to German transcription/source-completeness first: detect omissions, compression, and missing formulae before English translation; no native >=650 dpi Weber scan is currently on disk, with Band I/III around 500 dpi and Band II around 560 dpi, so hard symbols require tight crops and explicit uncertainty flags. The GitHub mirror carries the Weber workflow-method snapshot through Band I p401; later local logs extend the content map through Vol. I p648 and now show Phase 2 coherent re-transcription for sections 141, 148, 149, 151, 153-156, 158, 162, 163, 165, 167-183, with sections 171-172 re-verified as genuine map-phase transcriptions. Later author-staging packages add B139d p402-p407, B139e p408-p413, B140 p414-p467, B141 p468-p473, B142 hold evidence for p474-p479, and B143 p480-p485 / section 150 re-transcription as author-record staging; these later ranges and the 2026-07-02 Phase 2 workpass are not yet folded into the compact workflow ZIP. B143 and the later Phase 2 logs add practical guardrails: after a held or no-compile range, the next range still needs fresh source renders/crops/output checks; once a section is identified as fabricated or heavily compressed, slow manual page-by-page re-transcription in a controlled context can be safer and more token-efficient than repeated agent retries; an unusually fast all-clean report is a missing-scan/tooling warning, not evidence of correctness. The July 2 laptop Noether language-planning handoff, now mirrored through branch commit 6b983a15, adds another workflow lesson: source-evidence ZIP hashes, independent validation sidecars, Zenodo live checks, first-page contact sheets, French missing-unit matrices, Arabic/Persianate source-register shelves, and visual-triage ledgers are useful anti-regression and publication-hygiene gates, but they do not themselves promote a language branch or replace full visual/source inspection. Refresh the workflow packet before claiming p413+ Weber coverage, Phase 2 section coverage, Noether French completion, Noether Chinese visual clearance, or Arabic/Persianate term promotion inside the workflow artifact.

The addenda formalize the difference between OCR/source-witness aids, failed-run locator packets, working drafts, source-witnessed tranches, source-closed loci, critical editions, and unrelated local mathematical files that should not be published as part of this project.

Scope guardrail. Local sweep may inspect broad folders, but publication is limited to the manuscript transcription/translation/source-audit project unless Floris explicitly requests a named non-project upload. A file being mathematical, interesting, recently downloaded, or technically publishable is not enough.

Workflow status. The record is a reusable workflow packet, not a critical edition and not a claim that any particular mathematical edition is critically complete. OCR, VLM, detector, crop, candidate-TeX, derivative PDF, failed web-run transcript, source-inventory output, validation sidecar, and first-page visual-triage contact sheet are witness and locator layers unless a source-specific audit promotes them. Source scans and source-object witnesses remain authority for transcription claims.

Corrections and contributions. Workflow corrections, tool notes, reproducibility improvements, and issue reports can be suggested through the GitHub mirror via issues or pull requests: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/modern-latex-manuscripts.

July 2 source-ledger lesson. The SGA5 and Weber lanes now distinguish live local workpass cursors from compact promoted reader/delta packages. SGA5 local ledger now reaches p428 while the compact promoted SGA5 delta still stops at p260-p265; Weber local Phase 2 German workpass reached section 183 and 410 compiled pages while remaining non-English-synchronized and non-critical. The Weber pass also showed the mixed value of agents: they can locate severe reconstruction failures, but can hallucinate fixes on phantom/no-scan pages. The safe archive workflow is therefore locate, inspect the actual source scan, apply only source-confirmed edits, compile, render-check, record hashes, and publish public caveats. SGA5 p428 remains live-ledger/provenance status only; p427-p428 are clean/no-TeX-fix entries and p428 opens §6/§6.1 before any compact promotion.

Interlanguage methodology companion. A dedicated companion record now preserves the Slavic/Interslavic/constructed-language and terminology-governance apparatus at 10.5281/zenodo.21124403. It is linguistics/methodology material, not language-edition completion, native-speaker approval, source certification, or a critical edition.

Lean formalization sidecar companion. A dedicated companion record now preserves the compact Noether/Steinitz/Weber/Jordan Lean 4 / Mathlib-style sidecar package at 10.5281/zenodo.21129946. This is useful formalization/library-candidate material with build logs and Lean/Lake metadata, not proof of transcription correctness, source-fidelity evidence, translation certification, page-completeness certification, or a critical edition.

July 2 Noether R569-R574 source-control lesson. Noether R574 is the current packaged local TeX-changing German source-control head, R573 is the predecessor Paper 40 merge, R572 is the packaged no-patch tail-closure packet, R571 is the predecessor TeX-changing tail typography repair, R570 is the no-patch checkpoint, and R569 is the prior substantive p761/p764 repair head. This shows the same source-control pattern at small scale: source map, exact diff or explicit empty diff, two-pass compile, render check, README/audit/provenance ledgers, source witnesses, hashes, local ZIP, and caveated metadata under the Noether file ceiling. Workflow lesson: the source-control head can move faster than Zenodo's file surface, so publish exact public status and hashes promptly, but use compact curated rollups instead of scattering every micro-ZIP.

July 2 Noether R564 correction lesson. The initial R564 public nonpromotion was reversed after direct source rereading. The p731 witness uses x-family variables, so R564's chi-to-x/dense-formula repairs are source-matching. Workflow lesson: source witnesses govern both promotion and rejection; public metadata must be corrected when an audit call is shown to be backwards.

July 2 branch-handoff workflow lesson. The laptop Noether language-planning branch is useful but not merge-ready as a whole: a whole-branch merge would downgrade/delete current archive docs because the branch diverged. The safe workflow is commit-level/subtree inspection, compact source-intake receipts, and deliberate harvesting of specific sidecars/packages. Its current language-lane lesson is also public-facing: Slavic can be maintained as a watch lane; French still needs paper41, paper42, paper43, post44, post45, and postbibliography; Simplified Chinese and Japanese proof/render baselines still need full visual/source promotion before public-edition clearance; and Arabic/Persianate evidence remains corpus-first rather than reader-ready. This is not a language-edition completion claim.

July 2 Noether R573 follow-up lesson. R574 promotes a narrow Paper 30 p32 `auch` -> `stets` source repair above the R573/R572 predecessors without changing the public reader promise: it is source-control/support material, not a reader release, Noether closure, whole-corpus certification, multilingual synchronization, or a critical edition. The negative-closure lesson from R572 remains: non-corpus tail pages need source maps, page dispositions, hashes, and caveats so future agents do not waste effort re-transcribing publisher advertisements/blanks.

July 2 Weber sample-cert lesson. The Weber Volume I 20-page sample-cert audit is now 20/20 complete and failed as certification: §26/p90 and §164/p544 require full re-transcription, p400 and p580 content drops were fixed locally, 12 pages were clean, and §141-188 should be reverified page-by-page. Workflow lesson: repaired working editions need sample-cert and page-level audit labels because compile-clean, mathematically related TeX may still fail as transcription.

July 3 archive-maintenance object-class lesson. The latest sweep adds a sharper distinction between source-support, live ledger, active gap-pass, compact promoted delta, reader release, and critical edition. Noether R685/R686 are no-patch source-support/direct-audit packages and do not move the TeX-changing head; SGA5 p480 is a local French body-workpass ledger claim for a selected 10-exposé branch, not English synchronization or critical-edition closure; Weber Volume I p1-p76 is an active source gap-pass finding and fixing deviations, not a new reader release. GitHub and Zenodo metadata should preserve those object classes instead of collapsing them into completion claims.

notes: July 3 workflow refresh: no-patch source-support, live ledger/workpass cursors, and active gap-passes must remain distinct from compact promoted deltas, reader releases, critical editions, and source-certification claims. R685/R686, SGA5 p480, and Weber p76 are status/control evidence, not completion claims.
